text:
hana: Heads up for the weekly access review — ran the RBAC census for payments-service and found a possible KMS key policy mismatch for alias/k-payments-main. Policy shows two principals in the key policy that are not in our org owner list. Posting findings.

leo: can you paste the diff? curious if this is a stale partner grant or an actual misbind.

hana: pasted excerpt below (trimmed):
```
Key: alias/k-payments-main
KeyPolicy.Principal: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/partner-etl
KeyPolicy.Principal: arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/old-batch
Expected owners: [role:svc-payments-owner, role:infra-kms-admin]
```

priya: 999888777666 looks like the deprecated batch account we decommissioned in 2024. That should have been removed during cross-account cleanup. We should avoid immediate revoke until we confirm activity.

audit-bot: RBAC census job queued (id: rbac-20260401-07). Will attach the full export to S3 when complete.

david: quick vuln angle: if a key policy contains principals outside the verified list, it increases blast radius. Suggest steps: 1) check CloudTrail for any Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events from those principals in last 180d, 2) mark the key for manual recert if events present, 3) otherwise schedule policy patch with escrow.

hana: running cloudtrail check now for both principals. Command: ```aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=Username,AttributeValue=arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/old-batch --start-time 2025-10-01```

leo: FYI infra: noticed that KMS log ingestion had a delayed ship to the audit bucket last week; some events may be missing between 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-03. Filed INFRA-5567 for backfill. If cloudtrail comes back clean, we'll still want to keep the key in manual review to be safe.

priya: cloudtrail results: old-batch shows a single GenerateDataKey event on 2025-11-12 for svc:legacy-reporter. partner-etl has no activity in the last 365d. I'll attach the raw event id and snippet.

hana: attaching snippet: ```json
{"eventTime":"2025-11-12T03:21:09Z","eventName":"GenerateDataKey","userIdentity":{"arn":"arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/old-batch"},"resources":[{"ARN":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"}],"eventId":"e-abcdef12345"}
```

david: ok so there is one historical use. Treat as manual recert. Proposal: 1) add both principals to a temporary Escrow group for 7 days, 2) schedule policy patch to remove old-batch after 7 days if no new activity, 3) rotate the key material on approval. Thoughts?

leo: +1. Also request that we snapshot the key policy and list-grants before any patch and store it in s3://redwood-sec/recerts/1788005555/ for audit. Add a rollback playbook snippet.

hana: agreed. I'll capture pre-change state with: ```bash
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/k-payments-main --policy-name default > /tmp/k-payments-policy.json
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/k-payments-main > /tmp/k-payments-grants.json
```

priya: partner-etl — I can reach out to your inbox? Want to confirm whether the ARN belongs to a current partner integration before we start a 7-day escrow window. If partner confirms, we can formalize owner mapping.

partner-etl (external): thanks for ping. That ARN was from our old ETL pipeline; we migrated in 2025 and forgot to strip the original grant. We can confirm removal. No live jobs rely on it.

david: since partner confirmed, we can schedule a policy patch for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC with the following flow: 1) snapshot policy/grants, 2) add temp-escrow tag to key, 3) patch policy to remove old-batch, 4) run a smoke decrypt test from svc-payments-owner, 5) rotate key material if smoke succeeds. If smoke fails, rollback using captured policy file.

leo: add a step to notify #incidents and payments-owners 30m before the window and include SRE oncall. Also ensure KMS key rotation approval is recorded in the ticket.

sre-oncall: acknowledged. We'll monitor metrics and watch for elevated decrypt failures or job errors. Set alert threshold: >1% decrypt errors over 5m and paging threshold 5% over 5m.

hana: opening security ticket SEC-7892 with the plan and attaching the RBAC census export. Tagging owners @payments-product and @infra.

priya: follow-up action: schedule quarterly recert for all keys with cross-account principals and create a lightweight owner verification template. I'll draft the template and drop in this thread tomorrow.

hana: nice work team. Closing action list: - SEC-7892 created - INFRA-5567 follow up for log backfill - Patch window 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC - Evidence snapshots in s3://redwood-sec/recerts/1788005555/

david: recording a short rollback snippet here: ```bash
# restore policy
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/k-payments-main --policy file:///tmp/k-payments-policy.json --policy-name default
# restore grants (example)
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/k-payments-main --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/old-batch --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```

partner-etl (external): confirmed removal request submitted from our side. Thanks for coordinating.

hana: thread closed for now  will reopen if infra backfill returns missing events. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
